create.title: One-sided transform for the hard top M1 denominator block
create.statement_tex: Let y=floor(sqrt X), q=X/y^2, H=floor(yX^(-1/4)), and B_h=sum_(d<=y) chi_4(d)W(d/y)e(hX/d). Uniformly for 1<=h<=H, one-sided Poisson with full endpoint weight gives B_h=E_h^chi(X)+e(1/8)(hX)^(1/4)/i sum_(4h<n<16h, n odd) chi_4(n)W(sqrt(4qh/n))n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xhn))+O_W(log(2+h)), where E_h^chi=(2i)^(-1){e(hX/y+y/4)/(1-e(hq-1/4))-e(hX/y+3y/4)/(1-e(hq-3/4))}. The boundary denominators are uniformly separated; after the actual two-sided Vaaler weights the boundary is O(1) and transform errors are O_W(log^2 H). Multiplication by -4 alpha_(h,H) gives leading constant -2e(1/8)X^(1/4)/pi and reduces the top M1 block to M9-M1-top-endpoint-signed-cone.
create.next_action: Use the direct chi_4 partial-sum bound to close the endpoint block if possible; otherwise prove the exact signed M1 cone estimate.

create.title: Signed product-phase cone estimate for the top M1 block
create.statement_tex: For dyadic 1<=L<=X^(1/4), prove T_M1,L=sum_(h asymp L) sum_(4h<n<16h, n odd) chi_4(n)a_M1(h,n)e(sqrt(Xhn)) <<_epsilon L^(3/2)X^epsilon, with the actual normalized symbol a_M1 containing Phi(h/(H+1))W(sqrt(4qh/n)). Equivalently after swapping variables, the cone is r odd and ceil(r/16)<=m<=min(H,floor(r/4)). Together with M9-M1-top-endpoint-transform this implies the top M1 block target.
create.next_action: First test whether direct summation by parts against chi_4(d), before Poisson, already closes the unique top block; reserve this cone estimate for the residual range.

create.title: Exact piecewise product-phase kernel for the combined top M1/M2 contribution
create.statement_tex: After the exact one-sided M1 and M2 transforms and restoration of the H3 prefactors, their positive stationary parts have the common leading constant -2e(1/8)X^(1/4)/pi, common phase e(sqrt(Xrm)), and common outer character chi_4(r). M1 has r odd, m<=H, 4m<r<16m with symbol Phi(m/(H+1))W(sqrt(4qm/r)); M2 has r odd, r<=H, ceil(r/4)<=m<=r with symbol Phi(r/(H+1))W(sqrt(qr/(4m)). For r<=H the integer cones concatenate without gap or overlap, but the symbol is piecewise and M1 has an unmatched H<r<16H wing. The full contribution is twice the real part plus explicit target-sized boundary and transform errors. No estimate for this combined kernel is asserted.
create.next_action: Retain as exact infrastructure only. Do not replace the separate M1/M2 obligations by a combined estimate without an exact downstream bridge.

update.next_action: Build the direct M1 frequency phase diagram using bounded chi_4 partial sums and exact Vaaler weights. The top transform is proved, but its signed cone estimate and all lower/intermediate blocks remain open.
Prove the exact signed M2 affine-cone estimate. M1 has the same stationary sign but a different Vaaler variable and an unmatched wing, so cone complementarity supplies no cancellation.

reject.reason: The exact stationary constants have the same sign, so the adjacent cones reinforce rather than cancel.
M1 carries Phi on the inner original frequency and M2 carries Phi on the outer character frequency; the profile mismatch is order one near r asymp H.
The continuum reflection (r,m)->(4m,r/4) does not preserve the integer odd-r lattice, and M1 has an unmatched H<r<16H wing.
A bound for the sum of the two actual kernels gives no separate projection estimate without an additional stability lemma.

no_change.reason: The top M2 signed cone and the smooth-interior packet estimate remain open.
The exact transforms are known, but neither top signed cone is bounded at the required scale.
The final theorem remains conditional on open M9.

round_assessment.reason: Round 9 proves the exact M1 hard-endpoint transform and common product-phase architecture, while a blind derivation and hostile controls rigorously rule out the hoped-for M1/M2 cancellation.
